title: M5Stack emulator introduction video and CoreS3 virtual-device capture

firmware.family: UIFlow2 composed base plus same-VM live Python program
firmware.variant_note: UART live capture and web upload capture use distinct composed firmware images; neither identity is transferred to the other.

execution.environment: native QEMU through dedicated Device Service /api/v1; agent-owned session

media.qa: Full decode, real Chromium playback and 9 seeks, decoded-frame review, input before/after pixel check, encoded AAC loudness. See evidence/media-summary.json.

checks.detail: Used existing hash-bound runtime and firmware; no fresh runtime or firmware build.
Same guest program acknowledged by UART REPL; ready and touch serial markers observed.
Longpress (160,214), hold 1.0 s, settle 0.2 s; guest reports MODE 1.
138 captured PNGs, 137 unique hashes; guest demonstration changes state after input.
Virtual 320x240 framebuffer changes blue READY to green TOUCH ACTIVE; no physical measurements.
This capture uses native Device Service; browser execution is not inferred.
Separate a31ba1df firmware uploaded via current workbench; actual guest display visible and longpress changes READY to TOUCH ACTIVE; two owned sessions and service cleaned up.
Final MP4 produced and verified; media identity and scoped execution evidence archived. Publication performed after commit.

notes: Purpose-built visual demonstration; displayed wave is synthetic and not a measured sensor.
Product reference images and workflow graphics must be labeled as presentation material.
Only this CoreS3 firmware/runtime/program path is validated; no general compatibility or performance claim.
The film uses a crop of the actual workbench screenshot for seconds 35-46; guest framebuffer pixels are not replaced. Browser UI usage is not browser-WASM execution.
Media pixel-probe failures and correction are retained in media-summary.json; the MP4 binary was unchanged.

follow_up_executions.name: public workbench with local firmware upload
follow_up_executions.lane: browser UI -> native Device Service -> QEMU, not browser-WASM
